findings.message: The `deploy_result_in` path is extracted raw from attacker-controlled JSON via `jq -r '.inputs.deploy_result // empty'` and then used directly in a file-existence guard (`[[ ! -f "$deploy_result_in" ]]`) with no boundary check; an adversary who controls `ZBUILD_STAGE_INPUTS` content can supply a path to any world-readable file (e.g. `/etc/passwd`) and cause the guard to pass, making the plugin proceed as if a valid deploy result was provided.

`ZBUILD_DRY_RUN=1` is trusted as an environment variable with no integrity check, allowing any caller that can set the variable to bypass all health-probe execution and receive a `result_contract:2, verdict:healthy, disposition:complete` result — a full authentication bypass of the validation stage.

`ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR` is accepted from the environment and passed directly to `mkdir -p` and `atomic_write` without any path-boundary validation, so a caller that controls this variable can direct result artifacts to an arbitrary filesystem location (directory traversal / write escalation).

`hc_snippet` — the first 500 bytes of unchecked health-probe stdout — is interpolated into the stage-summary markdown without sanitization; probe output crafted to contain markdown or shell metacharacters can corrupt the summary or inject content visible to downstream consumers.

Clamping `return "$hc_rc"` to `return 1` silently discards probe-specific exit codes; if the health-check plugin uses distinct codes to signal security-relevant conditions (e.g. credential error vs. network timeout), callers lose that signal and cannot differentiate failure causes.
